review_notes: I read the whole file and the relevant parts of Mathlib/Order/Nucleus.lean, CompleteSublattice.lean and BoundedOrder/Basic.lean. I found no loops or competing-rule problems. The existing simp lemmas (mem_carrier, mem_mk, coe_inf, coe_himp, restrict_of_mem, range_toNucleus, mem_toSublocale) look consistent with each other. The two findings are about missing canonical rules. The round-trip lemmas are a fairly strong case because the file already proves their content inline. The coe_top finding is more modest. I could not run Lean, so I did not check whether the proposed lemmas would fire or compile. I also did not check whether adding them would change the behaviour of the existing proofs, such as the `simp [...]` calls in `Sublocale.instCoframe`.

findings.declaration: nucleusIsoSublocale (left_inv / right_inv proofs) together with Sublocale.range_toNucleus
findings.excerpt: right_inv S := by ext x; simpa using ⟨by simp +contextual [eq_comm], fun hx ↦ ⟨x, by simp [hx]⟩⟩
findings.problem: The file has two mutually inverse constructions, `Sublocale.toNucleus` and `Nucleus.toSublocale`, but no simp lemma for the round trips `S.toNucleus.toSublocale = S` and `n.toSublocale.toNucleus = n`. The only simp lemma nearby is `range_toNucleus`, which states the equality as a set range, not as a composite. The two round trips are therefore reproved ad hoc inside `left_inv` and `right_inv`, where `right_inv` repeats the argument of `range_toNucleus`. The only global statements, `eq_toSublocale` and `symm_eq_toNucleus`, are equalities of functions, so they cannot rewrite `S.toNucleus.toSublocale`. Any downstream `simp` on such a composite is stuck unless the user unfolds `nucleusIsoSublocale` by hand.
findings.proposed_change: Add two simp lemmas before `nucleusIsoSublocale`. `Nucleus.toSublocale_toNucleus (n : Nucleus X) : n.toSublocale.toNucleus = n` goes in the `Nucleus` namespace. `Sublocale.toNucleus_toSublocale (S : Sublocale X) : S.toNucleus.toSublocale = S` goes in the `Sublocale` namespace, and its proof can use `ext` and `range_toNucleus`. Then `left_inv` and `right_inv` can be closed by `simp`, and the lemmas also work for users. I did not check whether the first needs `Nucleus.ext` or `restrict_toSublocale`, which is the likely proof route. Both left-hand sides are composites of two constants and the right-hand sides are strictly smaller, so there is no cycle.
findings.benefit: Users and later files get a normal form that collapses the round trip. The two inline proofs in `nucleusIsoSublocale` become one-liners, and the duplicated reasoning with `range_toNucleus` disappears.

findings.declaration: Sublocale.coe_inf / coe_sInf / coe_iInf / coe_himp (coercion lemmas for the subtype instances)
findings.excerpt: @[simp, norm_cast] lemma coe_himp (a b : S) : (a ⇨ b).val = a.val ⇨ b.val := rfl
findings.problem: The file provides simp/norm_cast coercion lemmas for `⊓`, `sInf`, `⨅` and `⇨` on `S : Sublocale X`. It has no `coe_top` for the `OrderTop` instance `carrier.instOrderTop`, even though `⊤ : S` is defined as `⟨⊤, top_mem⟩` and the lemma would hold by `rfl`. The general `Subtype.coe_top` takes an explicit hypothesis `p ⊤` and an `OrderTop (Subtype p)` argument, so it is not usable by `simp`. This makes `((⊤ : S) : X)` a gap in the otherwise complete family. The sibling `CompleteSublattice` has `@[simp] theorem coe_top` for the same situation.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp, norm_cast] lemma coe_top : ((⊤ : S) : X) = ⊤ := rfl` next to `coe_inf`, after the `OrderTop` instance. Optionally add `coe_compl` (`(aᶜ).val = a.val ⇨ ⊥`), since `compl` is defined as `a ⇨ ⊥`.
findings.benefit: Simp can then reduce `(⊤ : S).val` to `⊤` in goals about the sublocale's frame structure. These goals currently stall, or have to be unfolded by hand with the instance, unlike the neighbouring `⊓` and `⇨` cases.
